_provenance.note: tgId 4 (AES-128, direction=decrypt), tcId 46. This ACVP 'isSample' release is small (4 groups x 15 tests, keyLen=128 only — no 256-bit-key group exists at all in this algorithm/release) and, of its two decrypt groups, only tgId 4 carries a non-zero payload: tgId 3 (ivLen=96, tagLen=128, aadLen=0) is fixed at payloadLen=0, i.e. tag-only/GMAC-shaped cases with no real ciphertext to decrypt. tgId 4 trades the default parameters for real content: ivLen=120 bits (15B, not the usual 96), tagLen=32 bits (4B, not 128), aadLen=120 bits (15B, non-empty AAD), payloadLen=120 bits (15B). All three non-default parameters are within SP 800-38D's legal ranges and within this engine's own accepted ranges — GcmState::new (rust/src/crypto/multipart.rs) derives J0 via GHASH for any IV length other than 96 bits per SP 800-38D §7.1 step 2b; aes_gcm_encrypt/decrypt (rust/src/native/encrypt.rs) only requires tag_bits to be a positive multiple of 8 up to 128; the C++ engine's OSSLEVPSymmetricAlgorithm equivalents are OpenSSL EVP_CIPHER_CTX-based (EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_IVLEN / EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_TAG), which natively supports arbitrary GCM IV and tag lengths in this range. tests/helpers.mjs's buildGCMParams and aesDecrypt were extended with optional aad/tagBits parameters (default: no AAD, 128-bit tag, so every other existing caller is unaffected) so this vector's AAD and 32-bit tag are actually passed through C_DecryptInit/C_Decrypt instead of being silently dropped; the KAT label in tests/acvp-wasm.mjs was corrected from 'AES-GCM-256' to 'AES-GCM-128' to match this release's real key size. Independently re-verified against Python's `cryptography` (OpenSSL-backed) Cipher(algorithms.AES(key), modes.GCM(iv, tag, min_tag_length=4)) with authenticate_additional_data(aad) before use: decrypting `ct` under `key` reproduces `pt` exactly and the 32-bit tag authenticates. Replaces a real-but-unprovenanced SP 800-38D / McGrew-Viega Test Case 16 vector (had a `source` citation but no `_provenance` block, so it still failed scripts/check_acvp_provenance.py) with genuine Tier-1 NIST ACVP material per the evidence ladder in docs/remediation-plan-pkcs11-v32-coverage-2026-08-29.md §1 — ACVP-AES-GCM exists, so it is mandatory over any Tier-3/Tier-4 citation. WS-0.5 of that plan.
